title: Dedicated capacity planning — 1:1 / weekly prep notes
content:
Meeting prep: Dedicated capacity planning (1:1 with Priya) — agenda + rough numbers

Date: 2026-03-04 (prep)
Owner: Ethan Park
Context: weekly sync / 1:1 focused on Q2 GPU pool forecasts, reservation ask for Dedicated, and autoscaling policy updates. Goal is to align on ask to finance + capacity ops by EOW so we can lock reservations and avoid 20% price increase risk.

TOP-LEVEL ASK (for discussion):
- Approve request to reserve additional 48 A100-80GB equivalents for Dedicated pools starting 2026-04-15 for 3 months (Q2 baseline).
- Approve temporary burst credit policy (10% of committed capacity) to cover spikes for 4 weeks post-launch of Retail Chat product.

ASSUMPTIONS (please challenge these):
1) Model mix for Dedicated customers next quarter: 60% instruction-tuned 70B class (multi-GPU sharded), 30% 13B-70B single-GPU variants, 10% embeddings/other small models.
2) Average sustained throughput per A100-80GB for chat workloads = ~90 tokens/sec for typical prompt+response mix (based on recent benchmarks).
3) Typical session length: 1500 tokens (prompt+response), average concurrency per customer route = 25 (peak).
4) Reservation target utilization target = 65% (we size for steady-state + buffer).
5) Pricing estimate: committed reservation (3 mo) approx $1.30/GPU-hour effective vs on-demand $1.85/GPU-hour (finance calc).

Rough demand calc (Q2 weekly baseline) — very rough:
- Peak concurrent sessions across Dedicated pool (expected) = 1,200 concurrent sessions
- Avg tokens/sec per session = 0.6 (after batching + caching) => total tokens/sec = 720
- Tokens/sec per GPU = 90 => required GPUs = ceil(720/90) = 8 GPUs for pure throughput (that seems low; accounting for model sharding/memory-bound 70B sessions, multiply by 6 factor) => adjusted required GPUs = 48 (matches ask)

Sensitivity check: if average session tokens/sec = 0.4 (less batching) => tokens/sec = 480 => GPUs = 480/90=5.3 -> adjusted w/ sharding = 32 GPUs. So 48 is conservative buffer for launch.

Cost delta (order of magnitude):
- 48 GPUs * 24h * 90 days * $1.30 = ~$135k (commit cost for 3 months)
- If on-demand at $1.85 -> ~$192k (delta ~$57k). Reserving saves ~$57k over 3 months.

Risks / open questions to bring up:
- Model mix might skew to larger models if a few enterprise customers request 70B+ with longer contexts -> could double memory footprint per session. How quickly can we spin up extra capacity?
- GPU procurement lead times and region constraints (APAC) — need to confirm preferred regions for customers.
- Autoscaler behavior: current policy scales based on pending queue length; for models with long init times (sharded 70B) warmup cost kills responsiveness. Need BKF (best known fix) — pre-warm warmed nodes for canary traffic.
- Cost vs quality: if we push customers to quantized variants to reduce GPU footprint, what's the expected quality degradation and allowed by SRE/SLA?

Proposed autoscaling policy updates (for discussion):
- Min pool size = committed GPUs for route (baseline); Max pool size = committed + burst_capacity
- burst_capacity = min(15% of committed, 32 GPUs) for Q2 launch window
- Scale-up trigger: predicted pending seconds > 10s for 30s window OR CPU/GPU utilization > 78% sustained 30s
- Warm pool for large models: maintain a small set of warm nodes with preloaded KV cache for top 10% routes (cost amortized vs latency wins)
- Graceful fallback: if desired model unavailable, route to compatible quantized model variant with scoreboard threshold checked (per Optimize recommendations)

Action items (clear owners & dates):
- Ethan: finalize reservation ask doc + finance justification, include cost-savings calc and risk section. Due: 2026-03-06. Linked: INFRA-3212.
- Priya: confirm partnership with Capacity Ops for APAC region mapping and lead times. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Marcus: prototype warm pool behavior and perf test (end-to-end) for 70B sharded sessions. Deliverable: perf summary + recommended warm pool sizing. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Alex: update autoscaler PR to include warm-pool flag and burst-cap policy. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/984. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Ethan + Finance (cc: Leila): confirm effective unit pricing on 3-month reservation vs monthly. Due: 2026-03-06.

Meeting questions (to ask Priya):
1) Is a 3-month reservation window the right ask vs 6-month? If sales signals strong, longer reservations reduce cost further but increase risk.
2) Can Capacity Ops support pre-warming for sharded 70B with KV-cache preload? Any operational knobs we should request from infra?
3) What telemetry should we share with Sales to justify reservation upfront (usage curve, customer commitments)?

Notes to self:
- Bring the small perf table to the meeting (copy below). Keep it light — focus on decision + one backup plan.
- If Priya prefers smaller reservation, propose tiered commit: 32 GPUs committed + 16 GPU burst contract at higher rate (switchable).

Quick perf table (from last week's bench runs):
Model | Per-GPU tokens/sec | Effective sessions/GPU | Notes
70B sharded (opt) | 90 | ~4 (sharded overhead) | warm-up cost 12s, KV cache helps 30% latency
13B int8 | 450 | ~20 | good for embeddings/chat single GPU
embedding-small | 2000 | n/a | batched inference highly efficient

Follow-ups after meeting: add final ask to Confluence + ticket to procurement (INFRA-3212) and sync with Sales on committed customers list.

Random TODOs / scribbles:
- Check DED-4321 for previous reservation terms and cancellation window.
- Ping Leila for budget sign-off thresholds for short-term reservations.
- Draft customer-facing note about planned Dedicated maintenance windows tied to reservation start.

End of notes.

(Informal / scratchpad style — will tidy before sending to procurement if approved.)
